newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends at day's peak but still lower.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends at day's peak but still lower.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures remained lower but closed at the session peak on Thursday as trade selling countered spec buying and industry interest on the dips.
"It's been a dead day," said one trader.
Trading was halted for about 26 minutes from around 3.30 P.M. local time due to a fire alert at the exchange. It later proved to be a false alarm.
By the close, September finished just $5 down at $1,860 per tonne after a low of $1,775.
July also rebounded from its lows but still ended $27 easier at $1,823.
London's decline was also slowed a lull in origin sales.
Origins, particularly from Indonesia, were noticeably absent. This prompted talk that the Indonesian crop could be considerably lower than most had expected.
Some said Indonesian exporters were also struggling to cover their commitments and this could give rise to problems of contract defaults.
New York, which took a tumble on forecasts of warmer temperature in Brazil's coffee belt, made some recovery on Thursday but the rise was short-lived.
Technically, London could remain in a wide $1,770-$2,000 range basis September before the next decisive move.
